title: Grateful Dead Live at Manor Downs on 1982-07-31
lineage: SRCS > WAV > Vegas 5 (matrix) > WAV > CD Wave > FLAC 16 (level 8)

ai_review.summary: A superb matrix recording captures a high‑energy 1982 show, highlighted by a smoking Scarlet > Fire sequence and crystal‑clear instrument separation.
ai_review.review: This release delivers an exceptionally clear matrix mix that lets every instrument shine, from Jerry’s soaring guitar tone to Brent’s fiery keys. The performance is consistently tight and energetic, with the second‑set Scarlet > Fire, Estimated, Eyes, Uncle > Truckin' and a sublime Morning Dew standing out as peak moments.

ai_rating.rationale: All reviews are overwhelmingly positive, praising both the musical performance (high‑energy, standout songs) and the matrix recording’s clarity; the weighted average of show (≈4.7) and recording quality (≈4.9) yields a near‑5 rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Superb matrix mix with precise, clean separation of instruments; balanced levels make every part easy to hear. Minor comment about early vocal wash, but overall crystal‑clear and well‑balanced.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set rolls with strong openers like Alabama > Promised Land, Candyman and a fiery Deal closer. The second set lifts off with Scarlet > Fire and flows through tight jams into an emphatic Morning Dew and a memorable encore of It's All Over Now Baby Blue.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for perfect guitar tone, soaring solos, and top‑notch vocals on Morning Dew and the Baby Blue encore.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for strong rhythm work and vocal delivery, especially on Bird Song and Estimated where his playing ‘tears it up’.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland’s keyboards add fuel to jams (e.g., Eyes into D/S) and are highlighted as clear and vibrant in the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drummers receive praise for tight, powerful percussion; the matrix captures the full range of percussive textures.
